steps.en: What you see: The walls thicken concentrically while the cavity stays normal in size. Ejection fraction stays normal until late in the course. The left atrium enlarges as diastolic stiffness rises. Long standing pressure load adds repolarisation changes that mirror the wall thickness.

Normal values with units: Wall thickness in diastole. Normal about 6 to 10 mm in men and 6 to 9 mm in women at end diastole.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular wall thickness

Left ventricular mass index. Mild increase 96 to 108 in women or 116 to 131 in men, in g per sq m. Moderate 109 to 121 in women or 132 to 148 in men. Severe above 122 in women or above 149 in men.. Source: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on left ventricular mass

Septal tissue velocity. Septal e prime below 7 cm per s or lateral e prime below 10 cm per s suggests impaired relaxation.. Source: ASE and EACVI 2016 diastolic function guideline, section on annular velocities

ECG and heart sound correlation ecg: Voltage criteria include a Sokolow Lyon sum of 35 mm or more from limb and chest leads combined, a textbook threshold outside the echo guidelines. Left axis deviation and lateral repolarisation changes follow chronic pressure load.
ECG and heart sound correlation sounds: A fourth sound marks the stiff ventricle. The apex beat is sustained. An aortic ejection sound in a young patient should prompt a search for valve disease.

What to report: Septal and posterior wall thickness with cavity diameter at end diastole
Mass index with the method and the body surface area used
Diastolic grade with left atrial volume index
Probable cause pattern: pressure load, athlete heart or asymmetric disease needing HCM review
Red flags needing urgent referral: Severe concentric thickening with heart failure symptoms, needs urgent cardiology review
Asymmetric septal thickening with family sudden death, needs HCM workup on referral
Aortic stenosis murmur with syncope or angina, needs urgent valve assessment
Pitfalls: Hypertension is the commonest cause in Indian adults, so record blood pressure control before labelling.
Athlete heart regresses with detraining while pathology does not, so ask about training load.
Amyloid thickens walls with low voltage on ECG, the opposite of hypertensive disease, so link echo to ECG always.

todo.en: How to get it on the probe, step by step: Start in the parasternal long axis and freeze at end diastole on the ECG R wave.
Measure septum and posterior wall thickness just beyond the mitral tips, excluding trabeculation.
Measure the cavity at the same level for the thickness to dimension ratio.
Move to short axis at papillary level and confirm the thickening is concentric all around.
Record mitral inflow and tissue Doppler because diastolic dysfunction follows hypertrophy.
Common mistakes and how to correct them: Measuring on an oblique cut that overreads wall thickness. Fix: Angle the beam perpendicular to the wall. Oblique cuts smear the wall and overread thickness.
Including trabeculation or a false tendon in the wall. Fix: Turn gain down and measure the compact wall only, leaving the bright trabeculation in the cavity.
Calling every thick wall hypertensive disease without considering athlete heart or HCM. Fix: Check athlete history, valve disease and family history before labelling hypertrophy as hypertensive.

remember.en: Link the ECG voltage and fourth sound to the echo.

q.en: What is the normal septal thickness band in men at end diastole?

why.en: Normal is about 6 to 10 mm in men and 6 to 9 mm in women.

why.en: Pressure load thickens walls concentrically while cavity size and ejection fraction stay normal until late disease.

q.en: Severe thickening is found with breathlessness and a loud murmur. What next?

o.en: Urgent cardiology review with blood pressure history
No action, it is always benign

why.en: Symptomatic severe hypertrophy needs urgent cardiology review for cause, obstruction and valve disease.
